W2 (empirical), after E048. Tip is E036: 5.314 s, 0.7532 on seeds 0-2. Identical-code reruns (E038 0.7525/5.334, E043 0.7497/5.294, E047 0.7544/5.343) show rebuild noise of about 0.3 pp on a 3-seed mean and about ±0.03 s on time. The population mean is about 0.752, so headroom over the 0.75 bar is about 0.2 pp.

Mechanisms, with the experiments that support them:
1. Epoch dial: about 5% of time per 0.5 epoch, for 0.0-0.25 pp (E020, E023, E027). E034 stacked the freeze with +0.5 epoch and saved 0.40 s versus E027 at about 0 pp.
2. EMA (+0.97 pp, E005) and Muon (+0.66 pp, confounded, E006) are in the tip. More than 10 time-neutral boosters failed (E025, E029, E030, E032, E044, wd, LS). Averaging, LR shape and wd sit at a flat optimum within about 0.2 pp.
3. Time tracks pixels. Early 20 px for up to about 30% of steps is nearly free (E026, E033). Trimming steps or samples costs about as much as the dial, roughly 1.5-2.3 s/pp (E040, E041, E031, E048). E048 (95% selection) saved 0.33 s for -0.14 pp, which is on the dial's line.
4. Backward truncation is the best lever (E028, E034, E036). It is bandwidth-heavy, because frozen blocks skip BN/GELU backward, the update and Lookahead traffic. E037 (60% freeze) cost 0.38 pp. E039 and E042 saved only 0.03-0.05 s. E046 (group-2 freeze for the last 10%) saved 0.24 s at 0.7540 accuracy, which is within noise.
5. Systems overhead outside the step graphs is about 2.5% (E047). Only identical-math changes can reach it, and gains are likely about half of it.
6. Noise: 3-seed std is about 0.15-0.2 pp. Any RNG or step-count change reshuffles it. Rebuilds change kernel selection.

Misses: E046 and E048 times came in lower than predicted; the savings from cutting steps or freezing are slightly larger than I model. E043 was rebuild noise. I over-predicted time-neutral boosters.

Unsure: whether E046's saving is real, whether it transfers to the PCIe judge, whether ReLU gives more than 3%, and whether the 0.25 epoch top-up recovers accuracy.

forecasts.reason: Freeze saves about 0.2 s and the top-up costs about 0.12 s, so net time is about -2.5%. Accuracy is near the tip, within noise.
Identical math. It may recover about 1-2% of time. Accuracy changes only through kernel reselection noise.
ReLU saves some elementwise traffic, about 2-3% of time. It likely costs 0.1-0.3 pp, which makes it roughly dial-neutral.

cruxes: Is E046's group-2 freeze saving of about 0.24 s real and accuracy-neutral on a same-build, 20-seed pairing?
How much of the 135 ms of non-step GPU work can be removed with bit-identical math?
Does ReLU's lower bandwidth cost recover more than the 0.1-0.3 pp it loses?
